fields.name: Name in the definition
fields.label: Label

auth.title: Sign-in
auth.lead: How nexdeck proves itself to the service. A key is never written here: name a field in braces, like {token}, and its value is taken from the connection.
auth.queryHelp: Name the field that holds the key, like {key}.
auth.loginHelp: A path below the address of the connection, such as /api/login. nexdeck never signs in anywhere else.
auth.bodyNested: This sign-in sends names inside names. The form cannot show that and leaves it as it is; edit it in the YAML.
auth.ticketHelp: The answer of the login: a field of its JSON, or a cookie it sets.
auth.ticketAtHelp: Where to find it in the JSON, like accessToken or data.token.
auth.passHelp: How the service wants to get it back with every request.
auth.passValueHelp: {ticket} stands for the ticket, for example Bearer {ticket}.

authExplained.none: The service needs no sign-in. Requests go out as they are.
authExplained.header: Every request carries a header with the key, such as X-Api-Key: {key} or Authorization: Bearer {key}.
authExplained.basic: Every request carries user and password as plain basic sign-in.
authExplained.query: Every request carries the key as a parameter at the end of the address. It appears in no log of nexdeck.
authExplained.session: nexdeck signs in once at a login address, keeps the ticket it gets and sends it along. On a 401 it signs in again once and asks again.

test.title: Test address
test.lead: What the Test button asks. It is green when the service answers well, and red with the reason when not.
test.pathHelp: A path below the address of the connection. A path in a subfolder works too.

reads.title: What nexdeck can ask
reads.lead: Addresses a card of this service may read, with a name each. They are offered in the Data step of the card editor.
reads.label: Name

preview.title: What whoever sets it up sees
preview.lead: The form for a connection of {{name}}, as it stands now.

extras.title: Extras
extras.lead: What makes it feel like a built-in one: the dot and the status page, the version it runs, and the project it is compared with. All of it is optional.
extras.checkHelp: The path nexdeck asks to tell whether the service is there. Left empty, the test address is used.
extras.versionPathHelp: The path whose answer names the version. It is read as JSON.
extras.versionAtHelp: The name of the field, for example version, or release.version for a field inside another.
extras.githubHelp: owner/name, or the GitHub address of the project. Its newest release is held against the version, only while Check for updates is on under System, About.
